Edit: removed some outright crap, added suggestion from @j_

It would be better to set the exact height and width on the ::after element instead of trying to match the padding and line-height to the image size.

e.g. 

display: inline-block;
padding: 0;
line-height: 0;
height: 96px;
width: 22px;

will fit your 96x22 image exactly. No need for fudging.

It might also be useful to identify what form of feminism causes you to feel anti-feminist or non-feminist.

From an academic standpoint, generally the idea of feminism is intended to incorporate women and the role of women into the dialogue, and to subvert paradigms that favored a strictly male narrative. As a sort of ham-handed example, there's a classic anti-feminist argument that men are better than women because there has never been a true matriarchy. While it's true that there never has been (and only pseudo-feminists try to argue otherwise, as well as fight for the idea of mother goddess worship, etc.), the idea that men are therefore 'better' rests on a paradigm that asserts that political or physical power makes one 'better' and more worthy of discussion. Of course, then you get into 'better at what?' and the like. A feminist perspective rejects these value judgments and is more interested in full incorporation of all genders and roles in the conversation.

And in terms of feminism addressing gender equality, the dispassionate starting point for a conversation is 'have genders ever been treated absolutely equally anywhere and at anytime?' I don't think you could ever say that's true. So where do we stand? And where are the lines of inequality? Where do we feel strong because of our gender? Where do we feel more helpless because of it? And these are all questions that are as honest and dispassionate as 'What is my favorite room in my house?' But once that passion, emotion, and hatred overrule logical analysis, the discussion of feminism gets silly.

So when someone says that there's a space to rationally discuss feminism from a non-feminist standpoint, from my perspective and experience it says that we want to rationally discuss the movement to incorporate women into a broader dialogue in an environment in which we don't want that to happen. So maybe define feminism a little more thoroughly? SJW feminism? Gamerghazi feminism? I don't know.
